title: Damp-Heat Stability of MAPbI3 Photovoltaics with Mesoporous TiO2 Scaffolds
notice: SYNTHETIC example, not real papers. Invented for pipeline demonstration only.

paragraphs.text: MAPbI3 solar cells built on mesoporous TiO2 scaffolds retained a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.7% after 500 h of damp-heat aging at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity.
Recent studies have reported MAPbI3 devices with initial PCE values above 21% under standard test conditions.
Moisture-induced decomposition of MAPbI3 into PbI2 is a widely recognized degradation pathway.
A mesoporous TiO2 scaffold was screen-printed from a commercial paste and sintered at 500 °C.
MAPbI3 was infiltrated into the mesoporous scaffold by sequential spin coating.
Damp-heat aging followed the spirit of IEC 61215: devices were held at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity without encapsulation.
The best aged device showed a PCE of 18.7% after 500 h at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity.
X-ray diffraction confirmed partial conversion of MAPbI3 to PbI2 after aging.
Devices built on compact TiO2 electron transport layers were not evaluated in this study.
The mesoporous scaffold appears to improve moisture tolerance by mechanically stabilizing the perovskite film.
Mesoporous TiO2 scaffolds extend the damp-heat lifetime of MAPbI3 photovoltaics; hysteresis behavior was not assessed.
